mission.title: cert-manager: Add ca.crt to TLS secret generated by ACME issuers
mission.description: Add ca.crt to TLS secret generated by ACME issuers. Requested by 37+ users.

steps.title: Check current cert-manager deployment
steps.description:
Verify your cert-manager version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n cert-manager -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cert-manager
helm list -n cert-manager 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working cert-manager installation.

steps.title: Review cert-manager configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant cert-manager configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n cert-manager -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cert-manager
kubectl get configmap -n cert-manager -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=cert-manager
```
The `ca.crt` field is added to the TLS secret generated by CA issuers, but is null for ACME issuers.

steps.title: Apply the fix for Add ca.crt to TLS secret generated by ACME issuers
steps.description:
If you are using a Let's Encrypt certificate for your openldap server, try configuring openldap to use the [Let's Encrypt root cert](https://letsencrypt.org/docs/certificate-compatibility/)  that is included in the container image:

```yaml
LDAP_TLS_CA_FILE: /etc/ssl/certs/ISRG_Root_X1.pem # CA
```yaml
*  https://hub.docker.com/r/bitnami/openldap/#Securing%20OpenLDAP%20traffic
```

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n cert-manager -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cert-manager
kubectl get events -n cert-manager --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "Add ca.crt to TLS secret generated by ACME issuers" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary:
If you are using a Let's Encrypt certificate for your openldap server, try configuring openldap to use the [Let's Encrypt root cert](https://letsencrypt.org/docs/certificate-compatibility/)  that is included in the container image:

```yaml
LDAP_TLS_CA_FILE: /etc/ssl/certs/ISRG_Root_X1.pem # CA file

# OR

LDAP_TLS_CA_FILE: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt # CA bundle
```
